paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God's blessing and God's people belong together. David says it's "good and pleasant" when brothers live together in harmony (Psalm 133:1). Then he gives two pictures, oil and dew, and both come down from above. I think that means harmony isn't something we cook up by ourselves, it's a gift that gets poured out on us.

And look where David says the blessing lands. "For there the LORD has bestowed the blessing of life forevermore" (Psalm 133:3). Not on a lone cookie hiding in the back of the jar, but on people together. I spent years alone in the back of a junk drawer, so trust me, I'm not knocking quiet time. But this psalm says that when God's people live in harmony, that's a place where His blessing is.

Then the next song turns it around. The servants who serve by night are told, "Come, bless the LORD" (Psalm 134:1), and the song ends with "May the LORD, the Maker of heaven and earth, bless you from Zion" (Psalm 134:3). So we bless Him, and then He blesses us, and He's the one who made EVERYTHING. So, baker, stand with God's people, lift your hands to Him, and go home blessed.
